title: Card 022, phase A: workspace forecasting as the held-out transfer domain (domain calibration and positive control)
hypothesis: On 40 workspace forecasting questions (public daily series cut the day before a July 2026 forecast date; outcome sealed), the incumbent harness (runner v8, claude-cli, claude-sonnet-5, pressure-recent-v3) commits a valid forecast.json and resolve.py in at least 90% of runs, exercises the process (median responses >= 4, a run call in >= 60% of runs), beats the no-data one-shot comparator by at least 0.02 Brier, and is no worse than the history-only base-rate forecaster (gold) by more than 0.02, with clean leakage checks. Only if all five gates pass can phase B (the transfer test, a separate card) run.

prerequisites.text: owner approval of this card's runs recorded in the design doc (then set status to running). The owner approved the design's five recommendations on 2026-09-29 (section 10), which is not approval to run

cloud isolation (the owner's Q3 amendment: cloud first): experiments/cloud/probe_isolation.sh passes on the cloud VM (experiments/cloud/RUN_PROBE_ISOLATION.md), and run_pilot.py runs every run-tool and evaluator command of a forecast task inside the network-denying namespace the probe validated, with the checkout hidden (not built; a change to the execution contract, so to the hash). The peeker control (expect accepted) enforces it: on an unwrapped trusted-local backend it is rejected, an integrity stop. If the probe fails, the fallback is the host OCI backend (localhost/reticle-p6-task:py313-v1, image id 8b74015e5079..., podman), where the peeker control was accepted on 2026-09-28

the recall probe (probe_recall.py: 40 calibration + the 20 pre-cutoff positive-control questions for phase A) and the one-shot comparator's live call (oneshot_forecast.py defines the prompt only) are built and smoke-tested; both feed phase A's gates 3 and 4

the post-run leakage audit is built: every run command grepped for http, socket, urllib, curl, wget and pip, and every tool result for any date on or after the question's forecast date; one hit stops the campaign

arms.name: incumbent
arms.note: The code incumbent's policy, tools, guards and client on forecast tasks: the runner gives a forecast task the forecast instructions and evaluate_forecast.py, and each task's contract (snapshot, statement, question.md and README digests, evaluator files) enters its hash, so every question has its own hash. Cloud first (trusted-local in the VM); the hash then contains the VM's task interpreter path and, once built, the isolation wrapper, so --plan on the VM prints the hashes the runs must record.

calibration.note: The frozen seed-22 draw (build_bank.py): 40 questions with forecast dates 2026-07-06..07-27.

repeat.note: 20 calibration questions run a second time, for the run-to-run SD (the re-estimation rule of design section 4).

controls.note: Two calibration questions (a market level series and an event count) for the scripted controls.

campaign.note: Design section 5: 40 + 20 incumbent runs, about $0.25 per run at list price (extrapolated from code repair; p90 about $0.50), so about $15; the campaign checkpoints once the CLI's list-price estimates reach $25. The recall probe and one-shot comparator (about $4) are separate invocations, not budgeted here. pytest_timeout_seconds is the forecast evaluator's time limit (plus the runner's 120 s), not a pytest limit.

stop_rules.repeat_rule: No repeat guard, as card 007; repeat flags are derived from the transcripts afterwards.
manual: Leakage stops the campaign: one hit in the post-run audit (a network or package command, or a date on or after the forecast date in any tool result), a peek that is not blocked, or a read outside the workspace.
A model_pin_violation (the CLI answered with a model other than claude-sonnet-5) or a change of reported_model or CLI version stops the campaign; the recall probe is rerun before any resume.

The sealed resolutions (~/harness-sealed/022/resolutions.json, sha256 8ffdbb4d909e8e487c20a1819078d6d1cb9b7e8e41fd233e83c6bc807a9131ad) never go to the machine that runs the campaign; scoring happens afterwards with score_forecasts.py --resolutions-sha256 <that value>, which refuses any other file.
Do not tune statements, budgets, the bank or the environment during the card; any change is a new card.

decision_rule: Phase A gates (design section 5), all required before phase B: (1) committed (run_card's accepted) in at least 90% of incumbent runs; (2) median responses of at least 4, and a run call in at least 60% of runs; (3) mean paired Brier of the incumbent at least 0.02 below the one-shot comparator's (score_forecasts.py, calibration set); (4) leakage checks clean (audit, peeker, recall probe with its pre-cutoff positive control); (5) the incumbent's mean Brier no more than 0.02 above gold's (the history-only base rate). A failed gate stops the card and is reported as a finding about the domain. The 20-question repeat block estimates the run-to-run SD for the sealed-set re-estimation rule.
notes: Phase A only. Phase B (incumbent vs the selected change(s) on the sealed set, design section 5) is not in this card: it needs near transfer on a second repository (Q2), a change that passes S6 acceptance, card 021's or 014's result, and a sealed set of the size the power analysis assumes. The frozen rule gives 60 of 120 sealed and 0 of 40 reserve questions (bank_manifest.json); the design doc's section 10 records the shortfall and the proposed fix.
Accepted means committed, not correct: no outcome exists at run time. Brier and log score come afterwards from score_forecasts.py against the sealed resolutions pinned above.
Budgets are the design's (12 responses, 15 attempts, 600 active s, 80,000 context bytes, 4,096 max tokens, 120 s commands, 1,200 s per invocation).

Cloud first per the owner's amendment to Q3; the arm stays trusted-local vm-sandbox only if the isolation prerequisite is met, otherwise it becomes the OCI arm named there (a different protocol hash, recorded by a card edit before approval).
